extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers/applicants seeking Medicare New Technology Add-On Payments (NTAP), health policy stakeholders, hospitals, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria used by CMS to assess FY2027 New Technology Add-On Payment applications (including alternative pathways for Breakthrough Devices, QIDPs, and LPADs), covering newness, substantial clinical improvement, cost, coding, authorization timing, and evidence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness criterion / newness period
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies must be within the 2-to-3-year newness period to be considered “new.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS determines the beginning of the newness period based on events such as FDA marketing authorization or commercial availability (examples: considers newness to commence on the date of FDA marketing authorization or on date the technology became commercially available). Technologies must be within this 2-to-3-year window to qualify for new technology add-on payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial clinical improvement criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The technology must represent an advance that substantially improves, relative to technologies previously available, the diagnosis or treatment of Medicare beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS evaluates whether the technology treats a distinct patient population unresponsive or ineligible for current treatments or demonstrates improved clinical outcomes compared to existing therapies. Lack of sufficient comparative evidence or inability to identify a distinct patient population can lead to disapproval (CMS notes head-to-head trials are not required but comparative evidence is needed to determine improvement). CMS invites public comment on whether the technology meets this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The technology must meet the cost criterion to qualify for NTAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reviews applicant-provided cost information and proposes a maximum new technology add-on payment typically calculated as 65 percent of the average cost of the technology (examples given for specific technologies). CMS may update cost information in the final rule based on additional information. Public comment is invited on whether the technology meets the cost criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not substantially similar to existing technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology must not be substantially similar to existing technologies for purposes of NTAP (unless using an alternative pathway).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considers whether existing therapies treat the same or similar disease/patient population and maps technologies to MS-DRGs. Public comments are solicited on whether a technology is substantially similar to existing ones; mapping to a new MS-DRG may support newness but similarity to other treatments can weigh against NTAP eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pathway eligibility for Breakthrough Devices, QIDPs, and LPADs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain alternative pathways (e.g., FDA Breakthrough Device designation, QIDP, LPAD), a technology may be considered not substantially similar to existing technology and need not meet the substantial clinical improvement requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologies using the alternative pathway still must be within the 2-to-3-year newness period and meet the cost criterion. Specific eligibility and timing rules apply (see FDA authorization timing requirement). CMS previously posted discussion and will continue consideration of issues identified with alternative-pathway applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA marketing authorization timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing requirements for FDA marketing authorization differ by alternative pathway category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Breakthrough Devices, applicants must have FDA marketing authorization by May 1 of the year prior to the fiscal year for which application is considered. For QIDPs and LPAD-approved technologies, authorization must be by July 1 of the year prior. CMS also describes a conditional approval policy for certain antimicrobial products under §412.87(d) where marketing authorization may occur after initial deadlines under certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a complete and active FDA market authorization request at application submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For technologies not already FDA market authorized for the indication, applicants (beginning with FY2025) must have a complete and active FDA marketing authorization request at time of NTAP application submission and provide documentation of FDA acceptance/filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet this requirement renders applications ineligible for consideration (CMS noted 7 of 32 alternative-pathway applications were ineligible for FY2027 for not meeting these requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility limited to the indication corresponding to the Breakthrough Device designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the use of the technology for the FDA Breakthrough Device-designated indication is eligible for NTAP under the alternative pathway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will only consider the designated indication for NTAP payment eligibility (examples: Ceribell, CARA, and CMORE—CMS questions or excludes uses outside the Breakthrough Device-designated indication). Applicants should clarify components/uses that correspond to the designated indication.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICD-10 coding and exclusion guidance for NTAP
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS identifies ICD-10-CM/PCS codes to report use of technologies for NTAP and may propose exclusions for combinations of procedure and diagnosis codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS posts tables (e.g., Table 10) listing relevant ICD-10 codes and may exclude cases reporting particular procedure codes combined with certain diagnoses (example: exclusion of cases reporting XX20X89 with status epilepticus diagnoses to distinguish different Ceribell products). CMS invites comments on appropriate ICD-10-PCS/C-M coding to identify the Breakthrough Device-designated use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and transparency of NTAP applications
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS publicly posts NTAP applications and supporting information online, except for confidential/copyrighted materials and certain cost/volume information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides links to MEARIS public postings for full applications and encourages public comment on applicant assertions and CMS preliminary assessments. Some detailed cost/volume/confidential information is excluded from public postings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence expectations for demonstrating substantial clinical improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS expects comparative clinical evidence to support assertions of substantial clinical improvement over existing technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While head-to-head trials are not required, CMS evaluates trial results, comparator data, statistical significance, durability, and whether outcomes (e.g., wound healing, pain, itch, safety endpoints) are improved relative to available therapies. Lack of comparative data or limited follow-up durations can prevent CMS from concluding substantial improvement (illustrated by CMS's review of ZEVASKYN where comparators and outcomes were insufficient to conclude improvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and measurement of clinical endpoints (example: wound healing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical endpoints should be clearly defined and measured consistently (example from applicant: wound healing categories and co-primary endpoints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant example: wound healing categorized as <50% healing, ≥50% to <75%, and ≥75% of baseline; ≥75% assessed as complete wound closure defined as re-epithelialization with no drainage or erosion and only minor crusting; co-primary endpoint evaluated ≥50% healing at week 24 with exploratory endpoints for ≥75%. CMS notes typical assessment by photographic and investigator visual examination in dermatology trials; routine biopsies are not standard and were not used for primary endpoints. Follow-up durations (e.g., 90 days, 6 months, multi-year) affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a large, chronic wound (RDEB context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant-provided definition: large, chronic wounds for RDEB generally means a wound greater than 20 cm² and open for more than 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reports applicant definition and uses it when evaluating claims about treating large chronic wounds, but considers whether existing therapies' labeling/dosing would preclude their use for such wounds when assessing whether the technology treats a distinct population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability of effect consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Durability claims (e.g., single, one-time treatment providing lasting benefit) must be supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS examines follow-up data and proportions of wounds achieving complete closure versus partial healing to assess whether a single application is sufficient. Evidence of partial healing or requirement for repeat treatment raises questions about durability and the asserted one-time treatment benefit (example: So et al. long-term follow-up showing mixed complete/partial healing outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-comparison requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of improved safety must be supported by comparative safety data versus existing treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS noted that applicant assertions of favorable safety (e.g., no treatment-emergent serious adverse events or no SCC reports) are insufficient without comparison to TEAE rates and SCC incidence with available treatments. Without comparative safety data, CMS cannot conclude an improvement in safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-per-case calculation issues for subscription-based technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies sold via subscription raise unique challenges in determining a cost per case for NTAP purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS acknowledges these unique circumstances, will continue to consider methods for calculating cost per case for subscription models, and welcomes public comment on appropriate methods, including whether cost analyses should be updated based on most recent subscriber data for each year of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum NTAP payment calculation (illustrative policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes maximum new technology add-on payments often represented as a percentage of the average cost of the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this proposed rule CMS used 65 percent of the average cost of the technology to propose maximum NTAP payments for illustrative technologies (examples: $61.84, $137.53, $10,205.00, $5,687.50, $2,171, $60,905 for various devices). CMS notes cost information may be updated in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility/ineligibility due to failure to meet program procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be deemed ineligible if they do not meet procedural or documentation requirements specified by CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 7 of 32 alternative-pathway applications were not eligible because they did not have the required FDA marketing authorization request documentation. Applicants must follow documentation deadlines and submission requirements described in regulations and prior final rules (citations provided).
